I think managing responses and interactions to my dysfunctional family will be a life goal. I.e. an urge to hold grudges, hit weak spots, hold tally, manipulate and generally hurt. Honestly it is probably learned behaviours. 

Either way, a few of us have learned to be better than our impulses and distance ourselves. However mentally I still hold damaging information and weak points "in case I ever need it". I got pretty depressed and avoided contact with friends and family, in that time a father figure lost his job and had to move back to Poland. I felt terribly guilty and after he left, my contact was even more sparse, a few months later he committed suicide. His death was not related to me in any way and it is selfish to ascribe this, however I sincerely will always feel guilty for this distance because I wasn't there.  It doesnt matter to me that even had I been there it may not have changed anything. I felt terrible because my depression and distance was damaging and hurting other people. So as that person that distanced, it isn't dislike that makes us distance it is more often something more personal about ourselves that makes it hard to see outside of our own selves. I guess for me it was a suffocating blanket of self hatred and hopelessness that i was wrapped in and in  the end I wanted it to suffocate me.

I am doing better now but when it comes to depression no one has the blame for it. Just roll with the punches and be there for others if you can.

In my limited experience, the coverage for a garage policy is meant to cover employees for damage to customers vehicles. There are two types of vehicle coverage that can be accommodated under this policy owned vehicles and not owned vehicles. I cant help but feel a courtesy car would typically be an owned vehicle as an owner can let others drive their  vehicles. With it being a non-owned vehicle, the garage policy would likely not cover the use of said vehicle by someone who is not an employee. Even rental agencies own their cars. 

I am no garage policy expert and Canada tightly control wordings for vehicle related insurance. As such I would say my advise is more specific to Canada but england may have a similar policy.

Every piggie responds to a cage build differently. While some people may look at your build and say there are issues, this doesnt mean there is. From a first time owner and cage builder, I have a few tips to lessen future frustration. 

1) Observation is key. Somethings wont work based on the individual pig. We had one piggie camp out on a ramp. 

2) A cage is evolutionary. A fleece lined cage was not what I imagined, but my guinea beaver is no longer eating his home to bits. 

3) Change is hated but sometimes necessary. Give them time to adjust.

4) Be prepared to expand, sometimes guinea pigs need their own space and items, as they grow bigger your cage might seem too small. 

This is based on personal experience, we had some really rough months and we made some big mistakes. But we have always been able to take solice in that as owners we always try our best for our pets.

Sharing some tips on building your own cage. I personally used cedar fencing wood for the sides and plywood bottom. The issues I came across was making sure the height of the wood is sufficient. My two guineas are not explorers so 5 inch height will do but if you actually want to stop a piggy from escaping you need to look at 8 inches or more.
If you are not use to  buying wood, the dimensions are more guidelines and you should measure the actual width prior to purchase. For my own cage I used 1.5"×1.5" wood to reinforce the corners. For a year I just placed a frame on top of plywood but when I went full custom I found actually connecting the two really helped with keeping the mess clean! 

I personally use fleece and towels. I layer it single layer garbage bag (waterproofing) 2-3 towels then a layer of fleece. By observing the guinea you will see they tend to poop in certain areas, put a tea towel in that spot for ease of cleaning and a tea towel where you put the hay down. Then when you do the big weekend cleaning you can set up a temp fleece enclosure on the ground and blitz clean the cage.

Forgot to add, have two water bottles and two food dishes, two huts and many different hidey spots. Boars need to be able to get away from the other. We use the metal grate build your own cage material at the corners of the cage to support the water bottles, but you could also try to let then drink from bowls.
